before.rappels: Descend the route: downclimb/short rappel off newer bolted anchors near the ridge crest back to the chockstone-chimney, then continue down the gully. The older Olympic Mountains climbing guide recommends two ropes.
before.descent: From the summit, reverse the exposed Class 3 ridge crest to the bolted double-anchor rappel station above the South Corner pitch and rappel back to the platform, then reverse the Class 4 gully and Cannon Hole squeeze down to Needle Pass. Descend the couloir (glissade-capable early season; expect an open moat and loose dirt/scree by August) to the Gladys Divide trail and Flapjack Lakes, then hike out via the Flapjack Lakes and North Fork Skokomish River trails. A single 60 m rope is generally adequate for the rappel, though some parties have carried two ropes to comfortably link stations.
gear: crampons & ice axe for the Needle Pass snow couloir (especially June–early July)
small-to-medium trad rack: wired nuts plus a few cams to about 2 in
60 m rope (or two shorter ropes) for the rappel
helmet — loose rock in the approach gully and at the Cannon Hole squeeze
